e-216.problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t) = 1+2t+3t^2+4t^3$. Calculate the acceleration of the particle at time $t=0$.
e-216.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $x(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+2t+3{t}^{2}+4{t}^{3}) \\  & =2+6t+12{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+6t+12{t}^{2}) \\  & =6+24t.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the acceleration at time $t=0$, we substitute this into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(0) & =6+24(0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the acceleration when $t=0$ is $6$.

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}-16t+15) \\  & =8t-16\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =8t-16 \\ 8t & =16 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =4(2)^{2}-16(2)+15 \\  & =16-32+15 \\  & =-1\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity when $a=0\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ is $-1\,\text{m/s}.$

content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2}+3t) \\  & =8{t}^{3}-2t+3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{t}^{3}-2t+3) \\  & =24{t}^{2}-2\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the acceleration at time $t=\frac{1}{2}$ second, we substitute $t=\frac{1}{2}$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{1}{2}) & =24{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}-2 \\  & =24\cdot \frac{1}{4}-2 \\  & =4\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
